info.name: Inji Certify With Mock Identity DPoP
info.description:
DPoP-constrained credential issuance (RFC 9449).

Uses its own environment, "ENV Mock Identity DPoP". Select it before running anything: a collection-level pre-request script checks env_flavor and aborts if the Bearer environment is loaded, for the reason described in that collection.

Environment ships pointing at a LOCAL deployment. To run the VCI flow against MOSIP's released deployment change these three variables only: authServerUrl, aud, relayingPartyId. Leave certifyUrl alone - it describes certify itself, which stays local whichever eSignet you point at. There is no audUrl in this environment: the OpenID4VCI proof audience comes from issuerIdentifier, which the collection-level pre-request derives from certifyUrl on every request, so it cannot drift out of step with it. That also means setting issuerIdentifier by hand does not stick. Registering your own clients on a hosted deployment additionally needs internalUrl and partnerSecret.

NOTE: switching to collab makes the Bearer collection work, but NOT this one. DPoP arrived in eSignet 1.8; the collab mock is older and issues tokens with no cnf.jkt, so every scenario here fails by construction. This collection needs an authorization server at eSignet 1.8+.

One scenario - DPoP scenarios / Token binding / unbound token with a valid proof - needs unbound_access_token, which only the Bearer collection can mint because only its client is registered with dpop_bound_access_tokens false. Copy that value across by hand; the scenario throws with instructions if it is empty. The other 25 need nothing from outside this environment.

DEMO KEYS: the RSA private keys in this environment are committed to a public repository and must be treated as compromised. They are for the local mock-identity demo only - never register them with an authorization server issuing tokens for anything real.

See docs/postman_collections/authorization_code_flow/data_provider_plugin/README-mock-identity-dpop.md.

exec: // This collection keeps its own environment. Selecting the other one would not
// fail immediately - the two share 20 variable names - it would run partway and
// write this flow's state into the wrong file. From OIDC Client Mgmt that costs
// a registered client: pm.environment.set CREATES privateKey_jwk in whichever
// environment is active, and eSignet cannot re-key or read back a client.
throw new Error('Wrong environment: this collection needs "ENV Mock Identity DPoP" (env_flavor=dpop), got ' + got + '.');
// The DPoP proof's htu claim must equal the URL the request actually goes to,
// byte for byte. Deriving these from certifyUrl on every request means changing
// certifyUrl alone is enough - the endpoints cannot drift out of step with it
// and start failing every proof with an htu mismatch.

item.name: OIDC Client Mgmt (DPoP)
item.description:
Registers {{dpopClientId}}, the DPoP client this collection authenticates as. Run it when you are standing up your own client - against the local docker-compose stack local-dev/dpop-test/setup-esignet.mjs has already done it, and ENV Mock Identity DPoP ships the matching private key.

The Bearer client wallet-demo is registered by the OIDC Client Mgmt folder of "Inji Certify With Mock Identity", from its own environment. {{dpopClientId}} carries dpop_bound_access_tokens: true and gives this collection its bound token; wallet-demo carries false and mints the unbound_access_token fixture that one scenario needs - see README-mock-identity-dpop.md for the one value that crosses between the two environments. They cannot share a key - eSignet enforces one public key per client and rejects a repeat with duplicate_public_key.

Request 3 generates its own keypair and writes the private half into the environment, so what it registers is immediately usable by the rest of the collection and nothing has to be pasted in by hand. The key lives only in that environment: keep it, and do not click Reset All afterwards, which would restore the committed demo key over it.

Request 4 updates an existing client's configuration - optional, and the only way to flip dpop_bound_access_tokens without registering a new client.

On a LOCAL eSignet client-mgmt is unauthenticated: skip request 1 and run 2-3. On collab and released it is a Spring OAuth2 resource server, so run 1 first and set internalUrl and partnerSecret.

// {status, message} and answers 200 whether or not a token was minted, so a
// green response here proves nothing. The cookie is the only evidence.
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

request.description:
Only needed on a hosted deployment. A local eSignet leaves client-mgmt unauthenticated, so requests 3 and 4 work on their own and this one has nothing to talk to - internalUrl ships empty.

partnerSecret is deployment-specific and deliberately not committed: set it in your own environment. A collab secret used against released answers 401 Unauthorized, surfaced as {"errorCode":"500","message":"401 Unauthorized: [no body]"}.

exec: // eSignet 1.8 (Spring Security 6, BREACH protection) returns the RAW token in
// the XSRF-TOKEN cookie and a MASKED one here. X-XSRF-TOKEN must carry this
// one; sending the cookie value gives 403 Forbidden with an empty path.
// Generates the keypair and writes the private half straight back into the
// environment, the same way the Bearer collection's Create OIDC client does.
// Nothing key-related is read from the environment first: this request produces
// the key material it registers, so it cannot be tripped by a variable whose
'pmlib_code is empty - no environment is loaded, or its CURRENT column is ' +
'blank. Select "ENV Mock Identity DPoP" and click Reset All in the environment editor.');
// Kept so a failed registration can put it back. On duplicate_client_id or a
// 401 the client that is actually registered is still the old one, and leaving
// the environment holding a key eSignet never saw would strand it.
// Written before the request goes out, so the environment holds the private
// half of exactly the key eSignet is about to register. Steps 2 and 6 of VCI (DPoP) sign their client
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
// The new key went into the environment before the request was sent. If eSignet
// did not take it, the registered client is still the old one - put its private
// half back rather than leaving the environment holding a key that exists nowhere.
// A 401 here has an EMPTY body - the reason is in WWW-Authenticate, which
// distinguishes 'Malformed token' from expired from insufficient_scope. None of
// the three appear in a body, so the header is quoted into the failure message.
// MOSIP reports registration failures at HTTP 200 with an errors array, so the
// status code above is not enough on its own. 'Full authentication is required
// to access this resource' here means authToken never reached the server: it
// goes in the Authorization header, and a Cookie: Authorization=... is ignored.
pm.expect(JSON.stringify(errors), 'duplicate_client_id means that id already exists with a different key - it cannot be re-keyed, so use a new clientId').to.equal('[]');

request.description:
Registers {{dpopClientId}} with dpop_bound_access_tokens: true - the one field this folder exists for. With it eSignet demands a DPoP proof at the token endpoint and stamps the proof key's thumbprint on the access token as cnf.jkt.

The pre-request script generates the private_key_jwt keypair and writes the private half to dpop_privateKey_jwk, so the environment is left holding the key of the client that was just registered and VCI (DPoP) works against it immediately. Do not click Reset All afterwards - that restores the committed demo key, which the client you just created will not accept.

Posted to client-mgmt/client, NOT client-mgmt/oidc-client. The v1 oidc-client endpoint silently drops additionalConfig, so a client created through it is never DPoP-bound and every scenario in this collection fails with 'access token is not DPoP-bound'.

Note the server profile also has to carry the DPOP feature; per-client dpop_bound_access_tokens only decides binding for a profile that supports it.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
// Same 401 shape as request 3: empty body, reason only in WWW-Authenticate.
// invalid_client_id means dpopClientId was never registered - run request 3 first.
// A field-name error such as invalid_status or invalid_uri means the body dropped
// one of the required fields: this is a full replacement, not a partial update.
pm.expect(JSON.stringify(errors), 'invalid_client_id means this clientId does not exist yet; a field error means the PUT body is missing a required field').to.equal('[]');
// Reported, not asserted: flipping this to false is a legitimate thing to do here
// - it is how you prove certify rejects a token that stopped being bound - so a
// test that demanded true would go red on the one deliberate use of this request.

request.description:
Updates {{dpopClientId}} in place. Optional - the flow does not need it. It is here for the one thing worth changing on an already-registered client: additionalConfig, and with it dpop_bound_access_tokens.

PUT client-mgmt/client/{client_id}, NOT client-mgmt/oidc-client/{client_id}. Those are different endpoints with different bodies - updateClientV2 takes ClientDetailUpdateRequestV3, the only update DTO that carries additionalConfig. Sent to the oidc-client path instead, the field is dropped exactly as it is on create, and the client silently stops being DPoP-bound.

This is a full replacement, not a patch: logoUri, redirectUris, userClaims, authContextRefs, status, grantTypes, clientName and clientAuthMethods are all required, and omitting one fails validation rather than leaving the stored value alone. The body below therefore repeats request 3's values verbatim - change the one field you mean to change. PATCH /client-mgmt/client/{client_id} exists for partial updates if you would rather not restate everything.

There is no publicKey field, by design: the registered key cannot be rotated and cannot be read back. A client whose private half is lost has to be replaced under a new clientId - re-registering the same one answers duplicate_client_id. So this request cannot repair a key mismatch, only configuration.

Flip dpop_bound_access_tokens to false and eSignet stops stamping cnf.jkt on the token: every scenario in this collection then fails with 'access token is not DPoP-bound'. That is a useful thing to prove deliberately, and easy to cause by accident.

item.name: VCI (DPoP)
item.description:
The VCI flow from inji-certify-with-mock-identity, run against the local eSignet 1.8.0 in local-dev/docker-compose.dev.yaml, with DPoP added. Run the requests in order.

Step 6 is where the binding is created: the client sends a DPoP proof to the token endpoint, eSignet verifies it and stamps that key's thumbprint on the access token as cnf.jkt, returning token_type DPoP. Nothing about the binding is simulated.

Step 8 then presents that token as 'Authorization: DPoP' with a fresh proof over the credential endpoint, which is what certify's DPoPProofValidator checks.

exec: // eSignet 1.8 returns a CSRF token here that is NOT the XSRF-TOKEN cookie value,
// and the header has to carry this one. Reading the cookie instead - as the
// published mock-identity collection does - gets a bare 403 on every later step.
// Every later request in the transaction is keyed by the transaction id and a
// The token-endpoint proof: htu is the token endpoint, and there is deliberately
// no ath - no access token exists yet for it to hash.
return dpop.proof({ key: walletKey, htm: 'POST', htu: tokenUrl, omitAth: true, nonce: nonce });
// RFC 9449 §8. eSignet ALWAYS rejects the first DPoP token request with
// 400 use_dpop_nonce and a DPoP-Nonce header; the request then has to be repeated
// with that nonce echoed in the proof. Rather than making you send this request
// twice, the challenge is drawn here with a throwaway call.
// It has to be the FULL token request. OAuthServiceImpl.getTokens runs
// validateRequestParametersWithTransaction before it looks at DPoP at all, so a
// partial form fails earlier and never reaches the nonce logic. The nonce is then
// stored against the hash of the authorization code, which is why this must carry
// the same code the real request will use.
// Nothing is consumed: verifyClientAssertionToken runs *after* the nonce
// challenge, so this assertion is never verified and its jti stays unused, and
// the code is not redeemed on a rejected request.
// Header lookup is spelled out rather than assumed case-insensitive, because
// a miss here is silent: the proof simply goes out without a nonce and the
// request comes back use_dpop_nonce with nothing to explain why.
for (var i = 0; i < names.length && !nonce; i++) nonce = res.headers.get(names[i]);
console.log('NO DPoP-Nonce CHALLENGE - this request will fail with use_dpop_nonce.',
// The two assertions that matter: eSignet honoured the proof and bound the token
// to the key that signed it.

item.name: DPoP scenarios
item.description:
One request per rule in RFC 9449 §4.3, each reusing a token from the VCI (DPoP) folder above and bending exactly one thing about the proof. Run that folder first. Order-independent, except the two replay steps.

One scenario - Token binding / unbound token with a valid proof - additionally needs unbound_access_token, which only the Bearer collection can mint and which lives in its environment. Copy it across by hand; see README-mock-identity-dpop.md. The other 25 need nothing from outside this environment.

// The bound token from the VCI (DPoP) folder, unless the scenario wants the
// unbound one, which is carried over from the Bearer collection by hand.
? 'unbound_access_token is empty. It is minted by the Bearer collection, which keeps its own '
+ 'environment: run that collection\'s VCI folder, then copy unbound_access_token from '
+ '"ENV Mock Identity Bearer" into this environment. See README-mock-identity-dpop.md.'
: 'access_token is empty. Run the VCI (DPoP) folder first.');
// signWith lets the proof be signed by a key the token is NOT bound to.
// The embedded jwk must be the signing key's, or the proof fails on signature
// before the binding is ever compared.
// Any string but the presented token proves the point, and a literal keeps this
// scenario independent of the Bearer collection's environment.
// The OIDC at_hash keeps the left-most 128 bits of the digest; DPoP's ath

// A repeated DPoP header reaches the server comma-joined.

// proof again - a fresh one would have a fresh jti and simply succeed.
